importance_ranking.reason: Roofing work has high visual sub-type variation — metal sheet vs tile vs polycarbonate vs PEB vs tensile fabric are visually distinct and non-interchangeable. Buyers scan images first to confirm the contractor works in their required roofing type; wrong type = immediate skip.

Roof material, service type (new/repair/waterproofing), service mode (labour+material vs labour only), and insulation type are primary shortlisting criteria — buyers eliminate listings that don't match their project requirement before contacting anyone.

importance_ranking.price_display_type: project-based price with per sq ft indicative rate
importance_ranking.reason: Indian construction buyers are highly price-aggressive and compare per-sq-ft rates across contractors before shortlisting; even though final price is project-negotiated, a visible indicative rate is a primary engagement signal and absence causes buyers to skip to the next listing.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Sub-segments vary: MS structural fabrication is quoted per kg/tonne; full shed turnkey projects are quoted per project lump sum; material-only supply may be per sq metre. Per sq ft is the dominant buyer-facing unit for service/installation contracts and must be shown to enable price comparison.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit — per sq ft vs per sq metre vs per project creates real confusion. Unit must be shown alongside price to prevent misreading.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant contractor brand with buyer recall exists in this category — market is fragmented across regional roofing contractors; buyers search by spec, location, and price, not by contractor name.
importance_ranking.reason: For larger industrial and institutional projects, buyers evaluate contractor track record, past project portfolio, and geographic service area during vendor selection — company matters but only after spec and price shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the roofing system IS — metal sheet vs polycarbonate vs concrete vs UPVC are non-interchangeable and drive the largest price delta across all spec dimensions in this category.

Insulated PUF/sandwich panel roofing commands a significant price premium over bare sheet roofing; buyers cannot substitute insulated for non-insulated and this spec drives the second-largest price delta within a given roof material type.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Project scale drives material quantity, labour cost, and per-sq-ft rate — sellers need the area to determine whether the project is within their operational capacity and to provide an accurate quote.
Whether the MS structural frame and purlins are included in scope (supply+erect vs roofing sheet fixing only) is a primary price and scope differentiator that sellers need to quote accurately.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines the roofing system the buyer needs — metal vs tile vs polycarbonate vs fiberglass are non-interchangeable and immediately route the RFQ to contractors with the relevant capability.
Building type determines structural load requirements, fire rating compliance, and project scale — sellers need this to confirm their capability and price the job accurately.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer wants labour+material supply or labour-only erection on buyer-supplied sheets — this fundamentally changes the scope, pricing, and which sellers can respond.
